newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour to force water firms to stem leakages.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour to force water firms to stem leakages.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party on Tuesday unveiled plans to force the country's privatised water companies to increase their investment in stemming leakages and promoting efficient use of water.

"The privatised water industry is repeatedly polluting the local environment, is making record profits on the back of falling investment and is failing to look after the interests of local people," environment spokesman Frank Dobson said.
"This is unacceptable. This must stop," he told a news conference.

Dobson said that if it wins the forthcoming general election, Labour would enforce mandatory leakage targets for water companies and require them to provide a free leakage repair programme for customers.
Labour would also make water firms offer free water efficiency audits of homes and promote development of water-efficient devices in the home.
But Dobson said Labour rejected the option of forcing people to install water meters.
"Water meters would be extremely expensive to install -- about four billion stg -- and to run -- a extra annual cost of 0.5 billion stg," he said.
"They could threaten public health and would bear most heavily on the most vulnerable groups, like pensioners and large families with low income." -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
